utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: A few moments ago, we saw a geographic map of Bosnia, and we saw that the Neretva River runs from Mostar all the way to the sea. Now, does this line actually correspond to the Neretva River basin from Mostar all the way down until the point where the river runs to the left, towards Ljubinje and Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take your proposition at its face that it does. I obviously am not in a position with this particular graphic to do a map-by-map analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler. Did you observe that those lines do not correspond and that the part of Republika Srpska is actually separated in that part, that it diverges, and that it did not come under the territory that was agreed under the Dayton Accords, because it says there the "Dayton line"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take it from your question that what you're asking is: Have I noticed that as a result of Dayton, territory that was once under the control of the Republika Srpska is now part of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: That's correct, thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you please take a look at the north-eastern part of Bosnia to determine whether the corridor between the Federation and Republika Srpska in the north-eastern part is rather narrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In directive number 6, is it possible that that part of the north-eastern part is referred to where it says that the borders of Republika Srpska should be extended in its north-eastern part in order to enable it to establish firmer ties with the Republic of Serbia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that the issue with what was known during the conflict as the Posavina corridor and the efforts by the VRS to continue to widen that particular corridor were of great significance. One can look at this particular map and clearly see that the narrowness of the corridor has a certain -- or lends to a certain threat that could be exerted to split the Republika Srpska into two. So in the context of that particular document, it certainly is possible that directive 6, especially if one were to go look at the tasks of the East Bosnia Corps, would have to do with the Posavina corridor. Again, rather than run right off of memory of directive 6 which I haven't seen for many years, I would again refer to the fact that the tasks related to the East Bosnia Corps would be in directive 6, defining this in some detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back to 65 ter 0481 which is the directive. It has now been adopted -- rather, admitted into evidence as D300. Thank you. We can see again that the document was issued on the 11th of November, 1993. As we already saw, the document that you called directive was published in the Official Gazette 15 days later, after this date, on the 26th of November, that is. My question to you is this: Is the directive or any directive drafted for one-half of a month or for a longer period, and would a longer period mean that the units bound by the directive are able to do something during that longer period of time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with your statement that the Official Gazette publication did come after this. How long a directive remained operative, in part, was dependent upon the relevance of the objectives and tasks laid out with respect to the situation on the ground. During the more fluid stages of the conflict in 1992 and 1993, directives were published in a period of perhaps three or four or five months, as necessary. At the end of the war, for example, directives 7, 8, and 9 were published within approximately an eight-month period. During this particular part of the war, from November 1993 through the publication of directive 7 in March of 1995, the situation - at least as far as the Republika Srpska was concerned - was relatively static. So in that particular context it's not surprising that directive -- operational directive 6 would remain in force for approximately a 16-month period.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us based on your research, does a directive cease to be valid when a new directive is issued, unless the second directive repeats a goal that was outlined in the previous directive?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of directive 6, for example, being superseded by directive 7, I would agree. However, in the context of looking at directive 7 and directive 7-1, it's clearly evident that directive 7-1 is not designed to supersede directive 7; it is designed to supplement it with additional and more detailed guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us what happened to directive 5 when the directive 6 was issued, the one that we see on the screen at this moment? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- is there a way to post directive 5? I mean, I'm not familiar offhand with the contents of directive 5. I mean, it is possible in the abstract that directive 5's guidance was reiterated in directive 6, but not seeing directive 5 and not having my memory refreshed on it, it's difficult to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to show you directive number 5. However, I would like you to tell us as a military expert: Are directives issued as a result of a newly arisen situation and dealing with the problems of such a newly arisen situation? Is a new directive issued in order to deal with the current situation or to deal with the previous situation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of the VRS, the directives deal with the current and projected situation, and they're issued in that light. They're not particularly historical in nature with respect to the tasks that are issued to the units. Now, having said that, it is entirely possible that the tasks issued in a previous directive might be once again issued in a next-numbered-sequence directive if those objectives have not been achieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: If one directive has been implemented, does that mean that a new directive is issued? And why is a new directive issued in respect of the old one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: A new directive within this particular context could be issued under two circumstances or would be issued under two circumstances. The first one is that the situation on the ground in broad levels has changed to a point where the guidance contained in that directive is no longer relevant to what is actually happening. The second circumstance would be if the political direction or the political strategic military direction changed and might require more offensive or defensive operations or, you know, changing the character of the conflict. So those are the two situations where the VRS or the Supreme Command might issue a new directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can you tell the Trial Chamber whether a new directive is issued to reiterate an old directive, or is a new directive issued as a result of a newly arisen situation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that generally the directives are issued in the context of a -- some form of a change of circumstance. Again, that is not to say that for the tasks of specific units those tasks may remain the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let me give you a practical example. You studied Srebrenica and Zepa. Can we now see page 5, both in Serbian and in English, paragraph 3. We're talking about directive number 6. Thank you. Do you now see the part starting with "the Drina Corps ...," the third paragraph? Thank you. If you haven't found it yet, I'm going to read the paragraph for you. I quote: "The Drina Corps used some of the forces to maintain the blockade of enemy forces in the Zepa, Srebrenica, and Gorazde enclaves, constantly inflict losses on them and disrupt their communications, and put up decisive defence on the front towards Kladanj and Olovo." My question is this: Were the enclaves already areas where UN forces were deployed, and did they already enjoy the status of protected zones? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The UN forces were deployed in the Sreb -- sorry, Zepa, Srebrenica, and Gorazde enclaves. By November of 1993, they were designated safe areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that the reason why the first sentence of the third paragraph reads: "The Drina Corps used some of the forces to maintain the blockade of enemy forces in the Zepa, Srebrenica, and Gorazde enclaves ..."? Is that the reason why the maintain -- the blockade is maintained, because those areas had been proclaimed -- had been proclaimed protected zones and people should not be allowed to leave them?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that people should or should not be allowed to leave them. What I am aware of is the fact that - and as I've testified - that even within the enclaves, certainly the VRS was aware that the Bosnian Muslim military forces did not properly demilitarise and did conduct military operations out of them. As a result, notwithstanding the UN's declaration that they were safe areas, particularly the Drina Corps found itself in a situation where they had to maintain some of their military forces around the perimeter of the enclaves in order to counter potential military attacks out of the enclaves by Bosnian Muslim military forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did military forces in Muslim enclaves exit the demilitarised areas and inflicted losses on the population? Did they also do that in order to implement some other objectives that had to do with other theatres of war? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. First, at least with respect to Srebrenica, first Operational Group 8 and then later the 28th Infantry Division did conduct operations outside of the enclaves and attack military and civilian objectives that were in Bosnian Serb territory. It was well-known that the reason why these forces would attack was because they realised that they were tying down Bosnian Serb military forces or units that could be better utilised to meet the larger war aims on other areas of the battle-field. So the ability of the ABiH to tie-down what would in effect be almost four or five brigades of soldiers garrisoning the perimeter around the enclaves gave them a military strategic benefit versus what the VRS was seeking to accomplish.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were combat activities by the 28th Division contrary to the status that was accorded to the enclaves by the Security Council and the interests of the other warring side?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The enclaves were supposed to be demilitarised, and clearly the information that is available reflects that they were not. I'm not sure of the second part of your question, the interests of the other warring side. Are you referring to the interests of the ABiH -- or the BiH government?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We're talking about the interests of the demilitarised areas. Was it contrary to the interests and the status of the demilitarised area that was recognised by the enemy side and by the Security Council? So was it contrary to their own interests to leave the demilitarised zone and carry out attacks outside of it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- clearly the fact that they were not demilitarised had an impact on the civilian population residing inside the safe area. The -- I guess because the people residing inside the safe area were Bosnian Muslim, the question is whether it was in the interests of the government, the Bosnian government, that these safe areas were not demilitarised. And I guess the answer is best defined as: A calculated decision was made by the government that the military benefits enjoyed by keeping the ABiH military forces in the enclave armed and conducting military operations were greater than the potential negative impacts they would have on the Bosnian Muslim civilians residing in the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We will see what the agreement says about that. But before we look at it, could you please look at the tasks of the Drina Corps in the fourth paragraph. And can you tell us whether the Muslims in Srebrenica maintained contacts with Zepa as well as with Kladanj and Olovo. Are you aware of that from the research that you carried out? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'm aware and have testified that the Muslim military forces in Zepa and Srebrenica were in constant contact with each other, and the VRS of course recognised that by their ongoing efforts to seek to separate the enclaves and prevent that type of contact. I am also aware that there was, through the course of the conflict, many situations where soldiers from the 28th Infantry Division would use various paths or routes to leave the enclave and make their way to ABiH territory, and, at the same time, military weapons or supplies that could be carried on foot were brought into the enclave using those same routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. When a strategic goal is set out to prevent a military communication with Kladanj and Olovo, would you say that this is a legitimate strategic goal, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of seeking to prevent the 28th Infantry Division from receiving military supplies, equipment, and personnel, there's nothing inherently unlawful with that as an objective. Now, I guess maybe I should clarify because you didn't ask unlawful, you asked legitimate. So in a military sense, it would be a legitimate object.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I will help you clarify, but let me ask you this first: When we're talking about tasks given to the Drina Corps over the eight or nine lines, is there a reference to the civilian population in the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica or to the civilian population, in general terms? I'm talking about this directive that we in front of us at the moment.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There is no reference to civilian population in that particular portion of the directive, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we move on to the agreement on demilitarisation, I would like to invite you to share with us any more information that you have about the Drina Corps and this decision.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any additional information except for what it says in the document, sir. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, can we look at D21, Article 3. Let's see what this document has to say about demilitarisation. Thank you. This is the agreement, actually. Thank you. Now we can see it. You can see the title: "The Agreement on Cease of Fire," signed by Ratko Mladic and Sefer Halilovic. This is on the title page. And now let's look at the third page because you wanted to see the document. Let's see the third page then, Article 3. Article 3. We can now see 4. I apologise for having called up page 3, although I wanted page 4. Now we have Article 3 where it says: "Every military or paramilitary unit shall have to either withdraw from the demilitarised zone or surrender their weapons. Ammunition, mines, explosives, and combat supplies in the demilitarised zones will be handed over to the UNPROFOR." And my question is this: Does this show very clearly that the Muslim troops in the enclaves or in the protected areas were not allowed to keep any weapons or explosives or anything of the kind? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it clearly reflects the fact that there was an expectation that these types of war supplies and equipment, including weapons, would be handed over to UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we can have our next break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, we should have the next break now and we will resume at quarter after 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we now again see D300, please, the first and the last pages, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we have before us directive number 6, the first page. We've already looked at it earlier. Can we now see the last page, please. That would be page 8. Thank you. We see that it was signed by Dr. Radovan Karadzic as the supreme commander and that it was typewritten in one copy only. Now, item 8 says: "The decisions of corps commanders are to be submitted to the commander of the VRS Main Staff for approval seven days before a planned operation." My question is the following: When you studied these directives and other combat documents, did you also study this directive, directive number 6 when -- where you discuss the strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that I -- as part of my analysis, I did review this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us, if you know, why directives are produced in one copy only and why they are sent to commanders alone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I expect, because I'm not completely sure -- but I expect that the particular reason why these documents are tightly regulated is because they lay out in very well-defined terms what the political and military objectives are for the state and for the army during the relevant period. One of the things or one of the features that I've noted in these is that in most of these, rather than being classified "strictly confidential," these directives are classified as "state secret." So, again, I expect that the reason has to do with the sensitivity of these documents and the damage that would be incurred with respect to the ability of the army and the Republika Srpska to achieve its goals if a copy of this document somehow was compromised and made its way to the ABiH or HVO entities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it classified as state secret because it provides specific information on one's own units as well as enemy units, and so on? Or is it because it is forwarded to the commander exclusively because he would be in charge of carrying out the task, and if it were to be done via other individuals, then the commander himself would be unable to actually pursue it immediately. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree with your first assertion because I have seen other documents, for example, operation's orders produced by corps which are strictly confidential but also lay out the situations in one's own units. I know that the classification of "state secret" is higher than the classification of "strictly confidential." So because of that and because these particular documents in great detail lay out the political-military objectives of the Republika Srpska and VRS, that they are much more sensitive to the military to protect, hence why their access is limited to fewer individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see P1214, please. That's directive number 7. And I would appreciate it if we could see page 1 and then page 5 in Serbian and 4 in English, the last paragraph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we see the cover page, page 1. Then we can see what the Muslim armed forces are engaged in. And now if we look at the first paragraph, it reads as follows: "After the signing of the agreement on the cessation of hostilities and the cease-fire, the Muslims have begun reorganisation of their armed forces by creating operative and tactical manoeuvre units, divisions, intense training, manning up to normal levels ...," and so on. Now, in documents of BH army, of the BH army, did you come across this detail that in this year, in the spring of 1995, the Muslims began reorganising their armed forces and creating operative and tactical units? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure laid out in that language, but I am aware that - and I believe I've testified to the fact that - the ABiH military, specifically the 1st Corps in and around Sarajevo and even the 2nd Corps in Tuzla, had plans to launch significant campaigns which would, of course, adversely impact the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please then take a look at paragraph 4 which reads: "The Muslims are planning a spring offensive along selected lines of attack in the direction of Sipovo, Srbobran, Vlasic, Teslic, Doboj, Brcko, Majevica, Kozluk, Sekovici, Vlasenica, and Han Pijesak." And then it says: "Trnovo, Olovo, Trnovo, Borci Krupa, on the Una river and Ripac." Can you recognise any of their offensive activities as part of the spring offensive in the territories which you did research on, such as Zepa and Srebrenica, if you're not aware of other areas? Do these place names mean anything to you? Do they ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and they would correspond to logical military objectives by the ABiH 1st and 2nd Corps. Most of these names are in the 2nd Corps area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you referring to the 2nd Corps of the BH army or of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: BH army, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And does the mention of Sekovici, Vlasenica, Han Pijesak say anything to you about the areas that you are aware of; in other words, Sekovici, Vlasenica, and Han Pijesak, do those names mean anything? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, those particular names are a part of the Drina Corps' zone, particularly in places like Vlasenica where it would bump up against ABiH 2 Corps. So those particular areas are where one's going to expect -- when you talk about from Zvornik south, you're talking about areas where ABiH 2 Corps and the Drina Corps are going to be, you know, in direct confrontation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was -- was the 2nd Corps in Sekovici, or was it a VRS army unit, and do you know which units were in Sekovici, Vlasenica, and Han Pijesak and which army they belonged to? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sekovici was the municipality and the unit there was the 1st Birac Brigade of the VRS Drina Corps. Vlasenica was the light infantry brigade, also of the Drina Corps. And Han Pijesak was not part of the Drina Corps area but was, in fact, the garrison location for the VRS Main Staff. One unit that it was and around that area was the 65 Protection Regiment, which is a Main Staff asset.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember whether there was a garrison higher or of more significance than the Vlasenica Brigade in Han Pijesak -- command of greater significance than the Vlasenica Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about in Vlasenica, the Drina Corps command was also headquartered in Vlasenica. If you're talking about Han Pijesak, that was the headquarters of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we see here that this assessment mentions the places where the main commands of those brigades and Main Staff commands were. Now, if we look at page 5 in English, we see the intentions of the BH army, the probable objectives and plans. And it says - we can see that in paragraph 3 from the bottom - in the second phase they will probably continue with their operations in order to take control of the rest of the territory of Republika Srpska and link-up the Muslim territories in order to create a unitary state in an attempt to link-up the enclaves, gain access to the Drina River, and then continue the attack in the direction of Jajce, Kljuc, and so on, in order -- with the aim of joining up the forces with the 5th and 2nd [as interpreted] Corps and seizing Borak and Nevesinje. This would enable them to carry out the offensive further towards the sea. Now, my question is: In the second -- at the second stage, is that what the Muslims did, in the second stage of their spring offensive, and I'm talking about 1995 towards the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is, in fact, not the third paragraph from the bottom but from the top.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am aware that towards -- that during 1995, particularly the spring, there were military actions undertaken by the ABiH to link-up to the ABiH 5th Corps, which at that time was isolated in an area known as the Bihac pocket. I don't believe that they were successful in finally doing that until August or -- I think mid-August or even late August before they ultimately realised those goals, but there was from -- literally from November 1994 onwards combat related to the 5th and 7th Corps out west, much of it involving the 2nd Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The directives state they will receive support from elsewhere, the Croatian side and other parties, including NATO. I did not read out that portion because then I would -- there would be a question as to why I'm reading that. But now I'm asking you whether Jajce, Mrkonjic Grad, Kljuc, and Sanski Most, whether these places are now in the territory of Republika Srpska or the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I'm referring to these places that are mentioned in the paragraph where it speaks about the second stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My geographic knowledge of that part of Bosnia is not so good that I would give you an answer off the top of my head without seeing a map. However, I think it's part of the historical record that as a result of the military operations by Croatia during Operation Storm as well as military operations by the ABiH forces in Western Bosnia, that a good deal of territory that was held by the VRS prior to 1 August 1995 was captured by them. I -- if General Tolimir were to say that those towns were lost as part of that, I wouldn't disagree with him. They did lose a substantial amount of territory during the period August, September, and October to those forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were those territories of Republika Srpska lost with the support of NATO air force and the land forces of Croatia and the BH army that captured it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The primary land component was the land forces of the Croatian army. NATO at the same time was engaged in an air campaign against the VRS related to what they perceived or what they justified as violations of the Sarajevo cease-fire in the heavy weapons area. I think history goes one way or another on whether or not NATO forces and Croatia operated in concert during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You studied documents. Do you know if the Security Council gave approval to the Croatian state to attack Bosnia and to NATO to support Croatia in that attack? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't study any documents related to that particular campaign. Again, the way the Office of the Prosecutor was organised, Operation Storm and the human rights abuses associated with that fell under the purview of a different investigative team and they had their own military analysts. So I have no knowledge whether or not the Security Council did or did not give any approval for any reason related to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, as I did already earlier in this trial, I would like to note that the Operation Storm and the war in Croatia or with Croatia is not part of this trial and not part of the indictment. Bear that in mind, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm talking about one part of the Republika Srpska. The Croatian Army was in the Republika Srpska occupying territories of the Republika Srpska and Bosnia. I'm not talking about Croatia. The witness also speaks about the Croatian Army in Bosnia and Herzegovina, i.e., in the Republika Srpska. The cities that are mentioned in paragraph 3 in English, the third paragraph 3 from the top in English and the third paragraph from the bottom in Serbian, were in the Republika Srpska, Jajce, Mrkonjic Grad, Kljuc, and Sanski Most. The Croatian army opened fire on those cities. They were occupied towards the end of the war -- or rather, they were taken towards the end of the war, which is exactly what the witness himself stated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, since we cannot discuss that part of the Republika Srpska, can I then ask you this: Did your research yield the result to the effect that the Muslims wanted to link-up the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa and that they also wanted to link-up the enclaves with the parts already under the control of the BiH army; for example, the territory under the control of the 2nd Corps headquartered in Tuzla. Were you able to ascertain that from any of the documents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't specifically look at detailed 2nd Corps documents on what their broader military objectives were in that context. However, I am aware from my studies of the VRS material that certainly the Drina Corps and, to an extent, the Main Staff, believed that those were the intentions of the ABiH army. Given the context of the actual battles and what had happened there from 1992 through to 1995, that's not unrealistic, that the VRS would believe that those were the goals of the ABiH in that area. And, in fact, it wouldn't surprise me if those were, in fact, the actual goals of the ABiH in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Exhibit P2369. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see the document. It says here the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Supreme Command Staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was issued in Kakanj on the 9th of November, 1994. The title of the document is "The Basic Plan for the Execution of the Task." And further on it says -- we will now read from this basic plan. If you look at the last line, you will see number 1 in English. The rest of the bullet point is on the following page; whereas in Serbian, we already have the entire bullet point on the page on the screen. I'm quoting: "The plan is to carry out active combat in order to liberate the temporarily seized territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina - the municipalities of Bratunac, Vlasenica, Sekovici, Zvornik, and Kalesija ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down because you are reading names of certain towns and villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I will repeat the names of the towns: "... Bratunac, Vlasenica, Sekovici, Zvornik, and Kalesija. And link-up the free territories of Zepa and Srebrenica with the free territories of Zvornik, Kalesija, and Zivinice, in order to create a permanent free corridor for the supply of the population and logistics support to the units of the BiH army and a basis for the further liberation of north-Eastern Bosnia as a whole." My question to you is this: This is a document sent by the Muslim side, does the Muslim highlight north-Eastern Bosnia as one part of the state that they wanted to liberate? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be what I would consider as my studies Eastern Bosnia, but their phrase and their use of the phrase "north-Eastern Bosnian" includes those specific towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We had a map on the screen. We saw what is meant by north-East Bosnia in geographic terms and we saw what that area meant to the Muslims. After we have read out bullet point 1 and the plan for combat operations, would you say that this confirms the credibility of the documents issued by various bodies in Republika Srpska in which documents the Serbian side refers to the Muslim plans and desires? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, it -- placing those two documents together in that context, you certainly are left with the view that the intelligence abilities of the VRS were functioning quite well and were able to accurately depict what they believed to be the strategic military goals of the ABiH with respect to how it lays out here. So in that particular context, the VRS was well-served by its assistant commander for intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the document that we have on the screen. Let's look at the second paragraph. There are five bullet points there, and the last bullet point reads: "The Chetnik decision" --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the previous page in English. I apologise. Thank you, Aleksandar. The previous page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Look at the last bullet point in the second paragraph where it says: "The Chetnik decision to attack your free territory before our joint active combat operations would compound the situation entirely, especially for you, if they would go for a direct attack against you. "With regard to the aforementioned, we propose that you think it through and give your proposals regarding the following basic plan and parts of the decision, whereupon we will send you the decision in its entirety, following which the preparations will need to speed up." My question: The Chief of Staff of the BH army, Hadzihasanovic, is the author of this document. Did he clearly express the Muslim intent to attack the VRS on the axis that I mentioned when I was reading from the document, including the one of the Main Staff of the Drina Corps and the other brigade, and that their goal was to liberate the territories of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that they intended to do that before the VRS was given an opportunity to thwart their intentions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I read it quite that way, sir. If you look at the first paragraph as a whole, what they're saying is that they have carefully studied the plan and they list a number of conclusions. When you look at these conclusions, they note several issues which are going to be problems, one of which is: We don't believe you have -- or what it says is: The forces that you have probably not sufficient to link-up. It notes that they're restricted by the use of the supply of -- or they're restricted by the supply of ammunition and other war materials. And also noting that a Chetnik or Bosnian Serb military decision to attack your territory before you carry these out would complicate your situation. Which then brings you to the last part of that first paragraph which is a -- essentially request back to them, saying that: We propose you think through and give your proposals following the basic plan of the decision, again saying: Please take into account the factors that we have raised, re-evaluate your plan, and determine whether or not the plan is still viable after you make these re-evaluations. That's how I read that particular paragraph in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this document a proposal made by the 8th Srebrenica group to the Main Staff, co-ordinated with the plan of the Main Staff -- actually, the document itself refers to a plan, does it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The document refers to the plan that was originated by OG 8 and reflects the fact that the plan has been reviewed, and in co-ordination with the 2nd Corps, there are a number of conclusions. It certainly was a practice, both in the VRS as well as the ABiH, that formations would be asked to create a plan and that that plan would be reviewed by higher headquarters. This document is a reflection of just such an activity, where the plan was apparently created by OG 8 and it was sent for review by various higher headquarters; and this particular document, at least this first paragraph, reflects some of the comments back from those higher headquarters to what they see are issues relative to the plan that must be re-thought or evaluated by OG 8 before a final decision can be granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we end today's session, can we see pages 10 and 12 in Serbian and English respectively. We are interested in bullet point 4.2 of the plan released by the Chief of Staff of the BiH army. He says here, and I quote 4.2: "The operation is very complex and requires relentless persistence and precision. It is complex to carry out and especially to prepare, and it requires a very great deal of persistence, where your place and role are irreplaceable and of great importance. With respect to the operation, devote yourselves to it to the highest degree with your associates, to whom you will occasionally give only extracts from your tasks, as and when they crop up and in the measure and scope required." Please, does it show here that they were given tasks and guide-lines in the measure and scope required and those needed to be implemented and carried out before the start of the operation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry to interrupt the General, but when we have -- could I ask that when we have long documents like this with specific questions that the -- Mr. Butler be given a chance to review the document before making analysis on -- or answers on particular parts of it? Because it's really important for a document to be reviewed in whole, I think, before an answer is made. Mr. Butler's obviously doing his best to be helpful here. But it should be -- especially for tomorrow, if there's a three- or four-page document if we can get the English and give it to Mr. Butler, he can probably get through it so we don't have to do it on the screen and take time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is a proposal for further dealing with these documents, but we are at the end of today's hearing. But we would like to hear your last answer. Do you recall the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but my actual answer was going to be the exact point Mr. McCloskey just raised. I'm really not comfortable commenting on a one-paragraph block on a 12-page document. There's a whole lot of -- I use the phrase "context" constantly. There's a whole lot of context in that document that I'm not seeing, so, again, Mr. McCloskey pre-empted my answer, which was going to be: I'd like to see the whole document and be able to read the whole document before I seek to answer General Tolimir's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence does not object to Mr. Butler receiving this document from the Registry in both English and Serbian and to be given an opportunity to study it before we resume tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it your intention to use this document in more detail during the examination tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Normally it's not the task of the Registry to provide hard copies for witnesses. Mr. Gajic, are you able to do that via the Registry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar kindly agreed to it, to do it - and I would underline it - on an exceptional basis. And then, indeed, Mr. Butler may use the whole night-time to prepare his answer for tomorrow. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is precisely what I had in mind. Mr. Tolimir and I have our own copies of the document, but they're practically unusable because we have jotted on them. That's why we are not in a position to provide Mr. Butler with his clean copy. Therefore, I suggested that perhaps the representative of the Registry could provide Mr. Butler with a copy. Whatever we would be able to do would be rather late in the evening, perhaps too late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. We are grateful for the Registry, for the assistance in this respect. We have to adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow in the morning at 9.00 in this courtroom again for the final session before the summer recess. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of July, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
